types.name: User data
types.desc: Caller's bytes: zfs_uio_t / iovec / page-cache pages. Uncompressed, logical.

types.name: DMU buffer
types.desc: dmu_buf_impl_t: one logical block of one object, held in memory (plus its dirty records).

types.name: ARC buffer
types.desc: arc_buf_t / arc_buf_hdr_t: cached block, keyed by DVA + birth txg.

types.name: Physical payload
types.desc: abd_t: the bytes exactly as they sit on disk (compressed / encrypted / padded to ashift).

types.name: I/O request
types.desc: zio_t moving through the pipeline (logical zio or a vdev child zio).

types.name: Block pointer
types.desc: blkptr_t: DVAs + sizes + checksum + birth txg. The address of a block.

types.name: Transaction
types.desc: dmu_tx_t membership / a txg number being opened, quiesced or synced.

types.name: Intent-log record
types.desc: itx_t / lr_write_t / lwb_t: ZIL records and log blocks.

types.name: Space
types.desc: Allocation state: metaslab class, DVA offsets, range trees, space maps.

types.name: Device I/O
types.desc: struct bio (Linux) / GEOM bio (FreeBSD): sector I/O at the block device.

types.name: Control
types.desc: Calls that carry no payload: locks, wakeups, throttling, accounting, callbacks. Draw dashed.

contexts.name: Open context: the calling thread (syscall / zvol worker), inside a dmu_tx
Syncing context: txg_sync thread or dp_sync_taskq workers, one txg at a time
zio issue taskq (z_wr_iss, z_rd_iss, z_fr_iss ...): CPU work - compress, checksum, allocate
zio interrupt taskq (z_wr_int, z_rd_int ...): completion processing
A dedicated kernel thread or zthr
Runs in whichever context calls it

groups.title: Consumers
groups.summary: Whatever issues the I/O: syscalls, mmap, zvol block I/O.

groups.title: ZPL - POSIX layer
groups.summary: Turns a file read/write into DMU object operations. Open context.

groups.title: DMU - transactions, dnodes, dbufs
groups.summary: Objects and their block trees in memory. Where data becomes 'dirty'.

groups.title: ZIL - intent log
groups.summary: Makes individual sync writes durable without waiting for a txg.

groups.title: ARC / L2ARC - cache
groups.summary: The block cache. Every buffered read and every dirty buffer lives here.

groups.title: TXG + sync context (DSL / SPA)
groups.summary: Groups all changes into transaction groups and pushes each to disk atomically.

groups.title: ZIO pipeline
groups.summary: The staged state machine every physical I/O walks through.

groups.title: Space - classes, metaslabs, DDT, BRT
groups.summary: Decides where a block lands and tracks free space and shared references.

groups.title: VDEV tree + queues
groups.summary: Redundancy layout (DVA copies, mirror, raidz) and per-disk I/O scheduling.

groups.title: Physical devices
groups.summary: What the I/O finally hits, by allocation class.

nodes.title: Application
nodes.role: Userspace process: write(2), read(2), fsync(2), stores to mmap'd pages, O_DIRECT I/O, copy_file_range(2), or block I/O to a zvol.

nodes.title: OS VFS glue (zpl / zfs_freebsd entry points)

ref.code: zpl_fsync(struct file *filp, loff_t start, loff_t end, int datasync)

nodes.role: Platform entry points. Builds a zfs_uio_t and calls the common ZPL code. ZFS does not use the OS page cache for read()/write(); only mmap goes through it.

nodes.title: ZVOL block device
nodes.role: A dataset exposed as a block device. Skips the ZPL and talks to the DMU directly, with its own ZIL.

nodes.title: zfs_write()
nodes.role: Loops over the write in block-sized chunks: quota check, start a tx, copy data into dbufs, update size/mtime, log the write to the ZIL, commit the tx. Returns with the data dirty in RAM; with O_SYNC/O_DSYNC or sync=always it then calls zil_commit().

nodes.title: zfs_read()

ref.code: zfs_read(struct znode *zp, zfs_uio_t *uio, int ioflag, cred_t *cr)

nodes.role: Takes a reader range lock, then copies from dbufs (or the page cache if the file is mmapped, or straight from disk for Direct I/O) into the caller's buffer.

nodes.title: zfs_fsync()
nodes.role: fsync entry: commit this file's intent-log records. No-op when sync=disabled.

nodes.title: Direct I/O decision
nodes.role: Decides per request whether O_DIRECT (or direct=always) can really bypass the ARC: the buffer and offset must be page-aligned, the range must not be mmapped, and a write must cover at least one full block. If so it sets UIO_DIRECT and pins the user pages. Otherwise the request runs as uncached I/O through the ARC (cached only until it completes), except that a misaligned O_DIRECT request fails with EINVAL when zfs_dio_strict is set.

nodes.title: File range lock
nodes.role: Per-file byte-range reader/writer lock. Serialises overlapping writes; appends and block-size growth lock the whole file.

nodes.title: mmap / page-cache bridge

ref.code: update_pages(znode_t *zp, int64_t start, int len, objset_t *os)
zfs_putpage(struct inode *ip, struct page *pp, struct writeback_control *wbc,

nodes.role: Keeps mmapped pages and the DMU consistent. Page faults fill pages from the DMU; writeback pushes dirty pages into the DMU; write() refreshes any cached pages. mmapped data is held twice (ARC + page cache).

nodes.title: zfs_log_write()
nodes.role: Creates the intent-log record(s) for a write and picks how the data is logged: WR_COPIED (data copied into the record now), WR_NEED_COPY (copied later, at commit) or WR_INDIRECT (block written to the pool, record carries its BP).

nodes.title: zfs_get_data() / zvol_get_data()
nodes.role: ZIL callback run at commit time to fetch write data that was not copied into the record: reads it (WR_NEED_COPY) or writes the block out via dmu_sync() (WR_INDIRECT).

nodes.title: zfs_clone_range()
nodes.role: Block cloning (reflink / copy_file_range): makes the destination point at the source's existing blocks instead of copying data.

nodes.title: dmu_tx (transaction)

ref.code: dmu_tx_hold_write_by_dnode(dmu_tx_t *tx, dnode_t *dn, uint64_t off, int len)

nodes.role: Declares what will be modified, then binds the change to the currently open txg. Everything dirtied under one tx lands on disk in the same txg or not at all.

nodes.title: Write throttle
nodes.role: Back-pressure. When dirty data passes zfs_delay_min_dirty_percent of zfs_dirty_data_max each tx is delayed progressively; at the max, writers block until a txg syncs.

nodes.title: dmu_write family

ref.code: dmu_write(objset_t *os, uint64_t object, uint64_t offset, uint64_t size,

nodes.role: Holds the dbufs covering the range and copies the caller's bytes into them. Full-block writes may hand over a pre-filled loaned ARC buffer instead of copying.

nodes.title: dmu_read family

ref.code: dmu_read(objset_t *os, uint64_t object, uint64_t offset, uint64_t size,
dmu_read_by_dnode(dnode_t *dn, uint64_t offset, uint64_t size, void *buf,

nodes.role: Holds the dbufs covering the range (reading them in if needed) and copies their contents out to the caller.

nodes.title: dmu_buf_hold_array_by_dnode()
nodes.role: Maps (object, offset, length) to a list of level-0 dbufs. Issues all needed reads under one parent zio and waits for them; drives prefetch.

nodes.title: Prefetch (dmu_zfetch)

ref.code: dmu_zfetch(zfetch_t *zf, uint64_t blkid, uint64_t nblks, boolean_t fetch_data,
dbuf_prefetch(dnode_t *dn, int64_t level, uint64_t blkid, zio_priority_t prio,

nodes.role: Per-dnode sequential-stream detector. Issues asynchronous reads ahead of the application so later demand reads are ARC hits.

nodes.title: Direct I/O write
nodes.role: O_DIRECT write: wraps the pinned user pages as an ABD and issues the block write immediately, bypassing the ARC and without waiting for txg sync. Only the block pointer is carried into the txg.

nodes.title: Direct I/O read
nodes.role: O_DIRECT read: reads blocks from disk straight into the user's pages. Uses the dbuf copy instead when a block is already cached or dirty.

nodes.title: dmu_brt_clone()

ref.code: dmu_read_l0_bps(objset_t *os, uint64_t object, uint64_t offset, uint64_t length,
dmu_brt_clone(objset_t *os, uint64_t object, uint64_t offset, uint64_t length,

nodes.role: Reads the source file's level-0 block pointers and installs them in the destination's dirty records as already-written blocks.

nodes.title: dnode (object)

ref.code: dnode_hold(objset_t *os, uint64_t object, const void *tag, dnode_t **dnp)
dnode_hold_impl(objset_t *os, uint64_t object, int flag, int slots,

nodes.role: In-core object: block size, levels, the root block pointers, per-txg lists of dirty records, prefetch streams. The root of the block tree a dbuf is found through.

nodes.title: dbuf_hold() + dbuf hash

ref.code: dbuf_find(objset_t *os, uint64_t obj, uint8_t level, uint64_t blkid,
dbuf_findbp(dnode_t *dn, int level, uint64_t blkid, int fail_sparse,

nodes.role: Finds or creates the in-memory buffer for (object, level, blkid). A new dbuf learns its block pointer from its parent (indirect block or dnode), which may itself have to be read.

nodes.title: dbuf_read()
nodes.role: Makes a dbuf's contents valid. Already DB_CACHED: nothing to do. Hole: zero-fill. Otherwise ask the ARC and wait for the callback.

nodes.title: dbuf_dirty() + dirty records
nodes.role: Marks a dbuf modified in a txg by attaching a dirty record, then dirties every ancestor up to the dnode. If the previous txg is still syncing the old contents, the data is copied first so that txg stays stable.

nodes.title: dbuf cache
nodes.role: LRU of dbufs nobody holds any more. Keeps decompressed blocks instantly usable; a hit here never touches the ARC. Evicting a dbuf releases its ARC buffer.

nodes.title: dmu_sync()
nodes.role: Writes one dirty data block to its final place right now, ahead of its txg, so the ZIL can log just the block pointer. The dirty record is marked overridden so txg sync does not write the data again.

nodes.title: itx lists
nodes.role: In-memory intent-log transactions, kept per txg and per object. They wait here until someone calls zil_commit(), or are dropped when their txg syncs.

nodes.title: zil_commit()
nodes.role: Blocks the caller until every record for the object is on stable storage. One thread becomes the writer; the rest wait on their commit waiter.

nodes.title: Log block builder (lwb)
nodes.role: Packs itxs into log write blocks. Pulls in write data through the get_data callback when the record does not already hold it.

nodes.title: lwb issue
nodes.role: Allocates the next log block (so this one can point to it), then issues this block as a rewrite of its pre-allocated location at sync-write priority.

nodes.title: lwb done + cache flush
nodes.role: After the log block is written, flushes the write cache of every vdev it touched, then wakes the threads waiting in zil_commit().

nodes.title: zil_sync() / zil_clean()
nodes.role: Once a txg is on disk its log records are redundant: advance the log header, free the old log blocks, drop the itxs.

nodes.title: zil_claim() / zil_replay()
nodes.role: Crash recovery. At import the log chain is claimed so its blocks are not reused; at mount every record is re-executed as a normal transaction.

nodes.title: arc_read()

ref.code: arc_hdr_alloc(uint64_t spa, int32_t psize, int32_t lsize,

nodes.role: Single entry point for reading a block by block pointer. Hit: hand back a buffer. I/O already in flight: wait on it. Miss: allocate a header and issue a zio (from the L2ARC device if the block is there).

nodes.title: ARC hash table
nodes.role: Header lookup keyed by pool GUID + DVA[0] + birth txg. A header may hold data (L1), only an L2ARC address, or nothing (ghost).

nodes.title: ARC states (MRU / MFU / ghosts / anon)
nodes.role: arc_mru: seen once. arc_mfu: seen again. Ghost lists: recently evicted, used to tune the MRU/MFU split. arc_anon: dirty buffers not yet on disk, never evictable. arc_l2c_only: data only on the cache device.

nodes.title: arc_buf (consumer copy)
nodes.role: The ARC keeps the on-disk form (compressed). A consumer gets its own decompressed, decrypted buffer filled from it, or shares the header's buffer when the block is not compressed.

nodes.title: arc_read_done()
nodes.role: Read zio completion: verifies and finalises the header, then builds a buffer for every caller that was waiting on this block and runs their callbacks.

nodes.title: arc_write()
nodes.role: Wraps a dirty anonymous buffer in a write zio. On ready the header learns the block's physical size, compression and checksum; on done the header is hashed under its new block pointer and becomes an ordinary cached block.

nodes.title: ARC eviction / reclaim

ref.code: arc_wait_for_eviction(uint64_t amount, boolean_t lax, boolean_t use_reserve)

nodes.role: Keeps the ARC at its target size. Evicts from the tails of MRU/MFU; headers move to ghost lists. Allocations wait here when the cache is over its limit.

nodes.title: L2ARC read
nodes.role: Reads a block from the cache device instead of the pool. On checksum or I/O failure silently re-reads from the pool.

nodes.title: L2ARC feed thread
nodes.role: Periodically copies buffers near the eviction end of the ARC lists onto the cache device, written as a rotating log.

nodes.title: TXG: open
nodes.role: The one txg currently accepting new transactions. Each tx holds it open (per-CPU count) from assign to commit.

nodes.title: TXG: quiescing
nodes.role: Closes txg N to new transactions (N+1 opens immediately) and waits for every tx still inside N to commit.

nodes.title: TXG: syncing (txg_sync_thread)
nodes.role: Takes the quiesced txg and writes it out with spa_sync(). Wakes on a timer, when enough dirty data builds up, or when someone waits for a sync.

nodes.title: Dirty-data accounting
nodes.role: Running total of dirty bytes per txg and pool-wide. Feeds the write throttle, triggers an early txg sync, and sets how many async writes each disk may run.

nodes.title: spa_sync()
nodes.role: Writes one txg. Repeats passes until nothing is dirty: writing blocks allocates space, which dirties space maps, which must be written too.

nodes.title: Uberblock + label update

ref.code: vdev_config_sync(spa_t *spa, vdev_t **svd, int svdcount, uint64_t txg,
uberblock_update(uberblock_t *ub, vdev_t *rvd, uint64_t txg, uint64_t mmp_delay)

nodes.role: The commit point. The new uberblock (pointing at the new MOS root) is written to every label; until then the on-disk pool is still entirely the previous txg.

nodes.title: dsl_pool_sync()
nodes.role: Syncs every dirty dataset in parallel, then dataset/directory accounting, then the pool's meta-object set (MOS).

nodes.title: dmu_objset_sync()
nodes.role: Syncs one object set: farms its dirty dnodes out to the sync taskq, then the meta-dnode, then the objset root block.

nodes.title: dnode_sync()
nodes.role: Applies pending dnode changes (block size, levels, frees) and walks its dirty-record list for this txg.

nodes.title: dbuf_sync_leaf() / dbuf_write()

ref.code: dmu_write_policy(objset_t *os, dnode_t *dn, int level, int wp, zio_prop_t *zp)

nodes.role: Turns each dirty record into a write zio whose parent is the zio of the block above it, and works out the write policy (compression, checksum, copies, dedup, encryption) from dataset properties.

nodes.title: dbuf_write_ready() / _done()
nodes.role: Ready (on an issue thread): the child's new block pointer is stored into its parent block in memory. Done (on an interrupt thread): space accounting, the old block is released, the dirty record is retired.

nodes.title: Block frees

ref.code: zio_free_sync(zio_t *pio, spa_t *spa, uint64_t txg, const blkptr_t *bp,

nodes.role: Copy-on-write leaves the old block behind. If no snapshot references it, it is freed in this txg, or queued and freed at the start of the next.

nodes.title: zio create + execute

ref.code: zio_rewrite(zio_t *pio, spa_t *spa, uint64_t txg, blkptr_t *bp, abd_t *data,
zio_read_phys(zio_t *pio, vdev_t *vd, uint64_t offset, uint64_t size,
zio_write_phys(zio_t *pio, vdev_t *vd, uint64_t offset, uint64_t size,

nodes.role: Builds a zio with the pipeline (a bitmask of stages) for its type and starts it. zios form a parent/child tree; a parent cannot finish a stage until its children have.

nodes.title: zio taskqs (issue / interrupt)
nodes.role: Thread pools per I/O type: issue queues do the CPU-heavy stages, interrupt queues handle completions. Sync writes use the high-priority variants.

nodes.title: READ_BP_INIT
nodes.role: Prepares a read: queues the undo steps (decrypt, decompress) to run on completion, decodes data embedded in the block pointer, or switches to the dedup read pipeline.

nodes.title: DDT_READ_START / _DONE
nodes.role: Read of a deduplicated block: read the normal copy; if that fails, try the other copies the dedup table knows about and repair.

nodes.title: WRITE_BP_INIT

ref.code: zio_write_override(zio_t *zio, blkptr_t *bp, int copies, int gang_copies,

nodes.role: Normally a pass-through. If the block was already written (dmu_sync, Direct I/O, clone) the supplied block pointer is adopted and the rest of the pipeline is skipped.

nodes.title: ISSUE_ASYNC
nodes.role: Hands the zio to an issue taskq so the caller does not burn its own CPU on compression and checksums. A write whose child blocks are not ready yet (an indirect block) is not dispatched: it waits here without a thread, and the thread that readies its last child carries it on into WRITE_COMPRESS.

nodes.title: WRITE_COMPRESS

ref.code: zio_compress_data(enum zio_compress c, abd_t *src, abd_t **dst, size_t s_len,

nodes.role: Waits for child blocks, then compresses. Tiny results are embedded in the block pointer, all-zero blocks become holes. Fills in the block pointer's properties and settles which pipeline the rest of the write follows.

nodes.title: ENCRYPT
nodes.role: Encrypts the payload and stores salt, IV and MAC in the block pointer. Pass-through for unencrypted datasets.

nodes.title: CHECKSUM_GENERATE
nodes.role: Checksums the final on-disk bytes and stores the result in the block pointer (that is, in the parent block).

nodes.title: NOP_WRITE
nodes.role: If the new data's strong checksum equals the block it replaces, keep the old block and write nothing.

nodes.title: DDT_WRITE
nodes.role: Dedup: look the checksum up in the dedup table. Known block: take a reference and skip the write. New block: write it through a child zio and record it.

nodes.title: DVA_THROTTLE
nodes.role: Chooses the allocation class and queues the write so only a bounded number of allocations per allocator are in flight. Only async-priority writes (txg sync) are queued: ZIO_PRIORITY_SYNC_WRITE writes (dmu_sync, Direct I/O), gang members, and classes with the throttle disabled go straight on to allocation.

nodes.title: DVA_ALLOCATE
nodes.role: Asks the metaslab allocator for space for each copy. Falls back to another class when one is full, and to gang blocks when no single free segment is big enough.

nodes.title: GANG_ASSEMBLE / GANG_ISSUE
nodes.role: Gang blocks: one logical block stored as a small header pointing at several smaller pieces. Used only when the pool is badly fragmented.

nodes.title: FREE stages
nodes.role: Free pipeline: drop a clone reference or dedup reference first; only when none remain is the space returned to its metaslab.

nodes.title: READY
nodes.role: The block pointer is final. Runs the ready callback and tells the parent, which is what lets a parent indirect block continue.

nodes.title: VDEV_IO_START
nodes.role: Routes the zio down the vdev tree. No vdev yet: fan out over the block's DVAs. Interior vdev: let mirror/raidz split it. Leaf vdev: align to the sector size and enter the disk's queue.

nodes.title: VDEV_IO_DONE
nodes.role: Waits for the vdev children, releases the queue slot, then lets the vdev type react (mirror: try another side; raidz: verify and reconstruct).

nodes.title: VDEV_IO_ASSESS
nodes.role: Decides what an error means. Only the logical zio (the one with no vdev) is retried, once, by re-issuing it down the whole tree; a leaf or interior vdev zio just records the error (ENXIO if the device is gone), may mark the device unable to write, and passes the error up.

nodes.title: CHECKSUM_VERIFY
nodes.role: Checksums what was read against the block pointer. A mismatch is counted against the device and reported so redundancy can supply a good copy.

nodes.title: DIO_CHECKSUM_VERIFY
nodes.role: Direct I/O writes only, on the first vdev child below the logical zio (the top-level vdev), and only when zfs_vdev_direct_write_verify is set (default on Linux, off on FreeBSD, which write-protects the pages instead): re-checks the user's pages against the checksum to catch the application changing its buffer mid-write. On a mismatch the block is not committed and the write is redone from a private copy of the data; EIO is returned only if that also fails.

nodes.title: DONE
nodes.role: Waits for all children, undoes read transforms, updates device statistics and error reports, runs the done callback and notifies the parent. An unrecoverable write error suspends the pool here.

nodes.title: Allocation class choice
nodes.role: Picks normal, special (metadata and small blocks) or dedup (dedup tables) for a block, from its type, level and size.

nodes.title: Allocation throttle
nodes.role: Per class and per allocator: admits queued writes in offset order while a slot is free, so allocation keeps pace with what the disks can absorb.

nodes.title: metaslab_alloc()
nodes.role: Allocates one DVA per copy, rotating across the top-level vdevs of the class so data spreads in proportion to free space.

nodes.title: Metaslab group / metaslab
nodes.role: Inside one top-level vdev: picks an active metaslab by weight and carves the segment out of its in-memory free-space tree.

nodes.title: metaslab_free()

ref.code: metaslab_free(spa_t *spa, const blkptr_t *bp, uint64_t txg, boolean_t now)

nodes.role: Records freed segments. Freed space is not reusable immediately; it passes through a deferral of TXG_DEFER_SIZE txgs first.

nodes.title: Space maps (metaslab_sync)
nodes.role: Persists this txg's allocations and frees as an on-disk log per metaslab. Being ordinary MOS objects, writing them dirties more blocks.

nodes.title: Dedup table (DDT)
nodes.role: Checksum to block mapping with reference counts. Lives in MOS objects, preferably on the dedup or special class.

nodes.title: Block reference table (BRT)
nodes.role: Extra reference counts for cloned blocks. Consulted only when a block is freed.

nodes.title: DVA fan-out (copies / ditto)
nodes.role: A logical zio has no vdev, only up to three DVAs. The mirror code treats those DVAs as mirror sides: writes go to all, a read picks one and keeps the others as fallbacks.

nodes.title: Mirror vdev
nodes.role: Writes go to every child. Reads go to the least-loaded healthy child; on error the next child is tried and the bad one is rewritten.

nodes.title: RAIDZ / dRAID vdev
nodes.role: Maps the block onto data and parity columns across the children. Reads normally touch only data columns; on a missing column or bad checksum, parity is read and the data reconstructed.

nodes.title: zio_vdev_child_io()

ref.code: zio_vdev_delegated_io(vdev_t *vd, uint64_t offset, abd_t *data, uint64_t size,

nodes.role: Creates the child zio for one vdev below. A child runs only the vdev stages; for reads with a known block pointer the checksum check moves down into the child.

nodes.title: Per-disk I/O queue
nodes.role: ZFS's own I/O scheduler, one per leaf. Classes: sync read, sync write, async read, async write, scrub, removal, initialize, trim, rebuild. Each has a min and max number in flight; adjacent I/Os are merged.

nodes.title: Leaf vdev driver
nodes.role: Converts the zio into the OS's block I/O request (Linux bio, FreeBSD GEOM bio, or file I/O) and submits it.

nodes.title: I/O completion
nodes.role: Device completion callback. Records the error and re-enters the pipeline on an interrupt taskq.

nodes.title: Label / uberblock writer

ref.code: vdev_label_sync_list(spa_t *spa, int l, uint64_t txg, int flags)
vdev_label_write(zio_t *zio, vdev_t *vd, int l, abd_t *buf, uint64_t offset,

nodes.role: Writes vdev config and uberblocks at fixed offsets in the four labels of each leaf, bypassing allocation.

nodes.title: Data disks (normal class)
nodes.role: Ordinary pool vdevs: file data and, without a special vdev, all metadata.

nodes.title: Special vdev
nodes.role: Metadata, optionally small file blocks and dedup tables.

nodes.title: Dedup vdev
nodes.role: Dedup table blocks only.

nodes.title: SLOG (log class)
nodes.role: Dedicated intent-log device. Holds only ZIL blocks, each for a few seconds.

nodes.title: Cache device (L2ARC)
nodes.role: Second-level read cache. Not part of the pool's redundancy; contents are disposable.

nodes.title: Labels L0-L3 + uberblock ring
nodes.role: Four label copies on every leaf: two at the front, two at the end. Each holds the vdev config and a ring of recent uberblocks.

paths.title: Buffered write, asynchronous (open context)
paths.summary: A plain write(2). The data is copied into a dbuf, marked dirty in the open txg and logged in memory. Nothing reaches a disk on this path.
paths.ends: Data sits in an anonymous ARC buffer with a dirty record; an itx sits in memory. Continue with path txg_sync.

paths.title: Partial-block overwrite (read-modify-write)
paths.summary: A write that covers only part of an existing block must read the block first. Shows the read path being pulled into a write.
paths.ends: Same end state as write_async, after one synchronous read. This is the cost of recordsize larger than the application's write size.

steps.note: read: one child is chosen
read: data columns only

paths.title: TXG sync: dirty data to disk
paths.summary: How dirty buffers become on-disk blocks. Trigger, quiesce, then spa_sync walks every dirty dataset bottom-up, runs each block through the write pipeline, and finally commits by writing the uberblock.
paths.ends: The txg is durable once the uberblock is on the labels. Waiters in txg_wait_synced() wake; the ZIL records for this txg are discarded.

steps.note: write: every child
write: parity generated, then every column
label and uberblock writes: physical writes to fixed offsets on each leaf

paths.title: Writes that never reach a disk (embedded, hole, nop-write)
paths.summary: Three ways a block write ends without I/O: the compressed data fits inside the block pointer, the block is all zeros, or the data is identical to what is already there.
paths.ends: The parent still gets a block pointer (embedded data, a hole, or the unchanged old pointer); no space is allocated.

steps.note: from here the block is written like any other (path txg_sync)

paths.title: Overwrite / delete: freeing the old block
paths.summary: Copy-on-write never updates in place, so every overwrite ends with the old block being released.
paths.ends: The space becomes allocatable again TXG_DEFER_SIZE txgs later, so a rollback to a recent uberblock still finds its blocks intact.

paths.title: Synchronous write / fsync through the ZIL
paths.summary: What makes one write durable before the txg syncs. The record (with its data, WR_COPIED or WR_NEED_COPY) is written to a log block, on the SLOG if the pool has one, then the device cache is flushed.
paths.ends: The caller returns. The same data is still dirty in the DMU and will be written to its permanent place by txg_sync; the log block is then freed.

options.label: write(2) with O_SYNC / O_DSYNC, or sync=always
WR_NEED_COPY: data fetched at commit time
WR_COPIED: data already in the record (no extra steps)

steps.note: shown with a single-disk SLOG; a mirrored SLOG adds the mirror steps of path read_miss

paths.title: Synchronous write, WR_INDIRECT (dmu_sync)
paths.summary: Large sync writes, logbias=throughput, and O_DIRECT. The data block is written once, straight to its final location in the pool, and the log record carries only its block pointer.
paths.ends: Everything from dbuf_dirty -> dnode onward happens later, at txg sync: the dirty record is already overridden, so only the block pointer is linked into the tree.

steps.note: dmu_sync() writes at ZIO_PRIORITY_SYNC_WRITE, so the allocation throttle is bypassed

paths.title: Crash recovery: ZIL replay
paths.summary: Sync writes that reached the log but not a synced txg are re-applied at mount.
paths.ends: Replayed changes are ordinary dirty data and go to disk with the next txg_sync.

paths.title: Buffered read, dbuf already cached
paths.summary: Shortest read path: the dbuf is still in memory with valid contents, so the ARC is not consulted at all.
paths.ends: A copy from memory to the caller.

paths.title: Buffered read, ARC hit
paths.summary: The block is in the ARC. The consumer gets a decompressed copy; no I/O.
paths.ends: The dbuf now holds the decompressed data, so an immediate re-read is a dbuf hit (path read_dbuf_hit).

paths.title: Buffered read, ARC miss, from disk
paths.summary: Full read path: a header is allocated, a read zio goes down the vdev tree to a disk, the checksum is verified on the way back up, and the block is cached.
paths.ends: The block is now in arc_mru. Indirect blocks on the way to it were read by this same path, one level at a time.

steps.note: read: the least-loaded healthy child
read: data columns only

paths.title: Buffered read served from L2ARC
paths.summary: ARC miss, but the header remembers an address on the cache device.
paths.ends: If the cache device returns bad data, wire l2arc_read -> zio_create (fallback) re-reads from the pool and the caller never notices.

steps.note: a physical read is aimed straight at the cache device's leaf vdev: no DVA fan-out

paths.title: Sequential prefetch
paths.summary: The prefetcher spots a sequential stream and reads ahead at async priority. Prefetched blocks land in the ARC without a dbuf.
paths.ends: A later demand read of these blocks follows path read_hit.

paths.title: Direct I/O write (O_DIRECT)
paths.summary: User pages are written to disk in the caller's context with no copy and no ARC involvement. The txg only has to link the finished block into the tree.
paths.ends: Compression and checksum run in the caller's thread. Everything from dbuf_dirty -> dnode onward happens later, at txg sync.

steps.note: Direct I/O writes at ZIO_PRIORITY_SYNC_WRITE, so the allocation throttle is bypassed
on the top-level vdev child, which carries DIO_CHECKSUM_VERIFY (for a plain disk that child is the leaf itself)

paths.title: Direct I/O read (O_DIRECT)
paths.summary: Blocks are read from disk directly into the user's pages; the ARC is not populated.
paths.ends: Blocks that were already cached or dirty are copied from their dbuf instead.

paths.title: mmap write (page-cache writeback)
paths.summary: A store to a mapped page only dirties the page cache. ZFS sees it when the kernel writes the page back.
paths.ends: From here it is an ordinary dirty dbuf (path txg_sync). msync / fsync adds path sync_zil.

paths.title: mmap read (page fault)
paths.summary: A fault on a mapped file fills a page from the DMU. The data then exists in both the ARC and the page cache.
paths.ends: Shown as an ARC hit; on a miss splice in the disk stretch of path read_miss.

paths.title: read() / write() on a file that is also mmapped
paths.summary: The extra work ZFS does to keep the page cache and the DMU showing the same bytes.
paths.ends: Writes update both copies; reads prefer the page cache copy because it may hold changes not yet written back.

paths.title: ZVOL write
paths.summary: A block write to a zvol. Same DMU and ZIL machinery as a file write, minus the ZPL.
paths.ends: Flush/FUA requests continue along path sync_zil; everything else waits for txg_sync.

paths.title: ZVOL read
paths.summary: A block read from a zvol: the DMU read path without the ZPL.
paths.ends: Shown as an ARC hit; on a miss splice in the disk stretch of path read_miss.

paths.title: Deduplicated write
paths.summary: After the checksum is computed the dedup table decides whether any data needs writing.
paths.ends: Duplicate: only a reference count changes. Unique: the block is written by a child zio. Either way the table itself is rewritten later in the same txg, on the dedup class if present.

options.label: New block: written by a child zio and recorded in the table
Known block: reference count incremented, no data written
Table unavailable or verify mismatch: written as a plain block

steps.note: the dedup parent zio: READY, then DONE
later in the same txg the dedup table's own blocks are written like any other block, on the dedup class if present (in every case, including duplicate)

paths.title: Read of a deduplicated block
paths.summary: A normal read wrapped in a parent zio that can fall back to the other copies the dedup table knows about.
paths.ends: The dedup table is not consulted on a successful read; the block pointer already holds the address.

steps.note: the child read runs ZIO_DDT_CHILD_READ_PIPELINE: no READ_BP_INIT
only if the child read failed: the parent is re-run and asks the table for the other copies

paths.title: Block cloning (reflink / copy_file_range)
paths.summary: No data moves. The destination's dirty records are pointed at the source's blocks and the reference table is told.
paths.ends: At txg sync the block pointers are linked in with no data I/O. Freeing either file later goes through the BRT (path free).

paths.title: Fragmented pool: gang blocks
paths.summary: No single free segment is large enough, so the block is split into smaller pieces behind a gang header.
paths.ends: Reading a gang block costs extra I/Os: the header first, then each member. Seeing this path busy means the pool is nearly full or badly fragmented.

paths.title: ARC eviction
paths.summary: Memory pressure or ARC growth past its target: buffers leave RAM, headers are remembered on ghost lists.
paths.ends: A later read of an evicted block is a ghost hit: a miss that also tells the ARC it evicted the wrong kind of buffer.

paths.title: L2ARC feed
paths.summary: Background copy of soon-to-be-evicted buffers onto the cache device.
paths.ends: The headers now carry an L2ARC address, which is what path read_l2arc uses after the data is evicted from RAM.

steps.note: a physical write is aimed straight at the cache device's leaf vdev: no DVA fan-out

paths.title: Read with checksum error: self-healing
paths.summary: A disk returns wrong data. The checksum catches it, redundancy supplies a good copy, and the bad copy is rewritten. The logical zio never sees an error, so no retry happens (that is path io_errors).
paths.ends: The caller receives correct data. With no good copy left, the read fails with a checksum error and the pool reports a permanent data error.

options.label: Mirror top-level vdev: another child is read
RAIDZ / dRAID top-level vdev: parity reconstructs the data
Extra DVA copies (copies=2/3 or metadata ditto blocks): the next copy is read

steps.note: ECKSUM: this copy is bad
read: the next child

paths.title: When I/O fails: retry, fallback, suspend
paths.summary: The error branches. A failed leaf I/O is not retried by itself: the error is passed up, and the logical zio above it is re-issued down the whole tree once. Then: a failed log write makes zil_commit() fall back to a full txg sync, an L2ARC read error falls back to the pool, and a data write that still fails suspends the pool.
paths.ends: A suspended pool holds every failed zio and re-runs it from the start once the pool is cleared (zpool clear).

options.label: Log block write to the SLOG fails
Pool data write fails on every copy

steps.note: the leaf I/O failed
a leaf zio is not retried: the error is passed up
the logical zio sees the error
the whole I/O goes down the tree again; assume the retry fails too

stages.name: DVA_CLAIM
stages.note: (not drawn: used only at import, to claim ZIL blocks)

pipelines.name: ZIO_DDT_READ_PIPELINE
pipelines.usedFor: logical read of a dedup block

pipelines.name: ZIO_REWRITE_PIPELINE
pipelines.usedFor: write to an already allocated block: ZIL log blocks, later sync passes

pipelines.name: ZIO_DDT_CHILD_WRITE_PIPELINE
pipelines.usedFor: the child that writes a new dedup block

pipelines.name: ZIO_VDEV_CHILD_PIPELINE
pipelines.usedFor: every child zio below the logical zio
pipelines.note: plus CHECKSUM_VERIFY for reads that carry a block pointer, plus DIO_CHECKSUM_VERIFY for Direct I/O write leaf children

pipelines.name: ZIO_INTERLOCK_PIPELINE
pipelines.usedFor: what a zio is cut down to when no I/O is needed: embedded data, holes, nop-write, override, dedup duplicate

pipelineRuntimeNote: NOP_WRITE is switched on in `zio_write_compress` when the block qualifies; the gang stages are added by `zio_create` for gang block pointers; WRITE_COMPRESS can switch a write to ZIO_REWRITE_PIPELINE on later sync passes (`zfs_sync_pass_rewrite`).

model: A write happens in two phases. In open context the caller only copies data into memory and marks it dirty in the currently open transaction group (txg). Later, in syncing context, a dedicated thread writes the whole txg to disk.
The intent log (ZIL) exists only to make individual synchronous writes durable before their txg syncs. It is never read in normal operation, only after a crash.
Every buffered block lives in the ARC, in its on-disk (compressed) form. Consumers get decompressed copies through dbufs.
Every physical I/O is a zio walking a staged pipeline. Which stages run is a bitmask chosen when the zio is created (Appendix B). Reads and writes share most stage code.
ZFS is copy-on-write and writes bottom-up. A block's address is only known after allocation, and it is stored in the parent block, so children are written first and the parent's checksum covers them.
The vdev tree is walked recursively: a logical zio spawns child zios per copy, per mirror side or per raidz column, and each leaf disk has its own priority queue.
A txg is committed by one small write: the uberblock. Until that lands, the pool on disk is entirely the previous txg.
simplifications: Pipeline stage nodes are shared by reads, writes and frees. Which stages a given zio visits is set by its pipeline bitmask (Appendix B); the paths show the common cases.

The vdev layer is recursive. A child zio re-enters `VDEV_IO_START` on the vdev below; the diagram draws this as a loop through `vdev_child_io`, and the return as the wire from `st_done` back to `st_vdev_io_done`.
"DVA fan-out" and "Mirror vdev" are the same code (`vdev_mirror.c`). They are separate nodes because they play different roles.
dRAID is folded into the RAIDZ node. Gang blocks, dedup and cloning are drawn in less detail than the main paths.
Device nodes are roles, not hardware. A pool with no special, dedup or log vdev sends all of that traffic to the data disks, and a pool with no cache device has no L2ARC wires in use.
Indirect blocks are not drawn separately. Reading or writing a data block also reads or writes the indirect blocks above it by the same path, one level at a time.
Locks other than the file range lock, and most statistics and error-reporting calls, are left out.

page.title: ZFS I/O Flow
page.intro: This document is a complete brief for an agent that will build an interactive diagram of the OpenZFS read and write paths, styled like a ComfyUI workflow. Sections 1 to 5 say what to build and how it must behave. Sections 6 to 10 are the diagram's content as tables: 99 nodes, 254 wires, 28 named paths. Sections 11 to 13 cover accuracy, build order and acceptance. Appendices A to D give the exact source file and line behind every function, wire, tunable and property, so that every item on the page links to the code it describes.
